findings.evidence: The generalized merge equations already occur at lines 266 and 308 with `[Finite (Quotient (SameCycle.setoid σ))]` plus periodicity, while the orbit-relation splitting theorem at line 225 likewise needs only periodicity. The current proof’s need to synthesize finiteness for the product quotient is a proof gap, not a counterexample to the more general statement: splitting one finite periodic orbit into two preserves finiteness of the orbit quotient.
findings.fix: Add generalized splitting lemmas using finite orbit quotients and explicit periodic-point hypotheses, then derive the existing `[Finite α]` `@[simp]` corollaries from them.
findings.issue: `orbitCount_swap_mul_of_sameCycle` and its right-multiplication counterpart at line 332 assume `[Finite α]`; the operation only splits one periodic orbit, so finiteness of the underlying type is stronger than necessary.

summary: The splitting half remains restricted to finite underlying types, unlike the generalized merging half, although only orbit-set finiteness and periodicity are mathematically needed.
